newsitem.title: USA: Kellogg to acquire Lender's bagels business.
newsitem.headline: Kellogg to acquire Lender's bagels business.

text.p: Kellogg Co said Monday it agreed to acquire the Lender's Bagels business from Kraft Foods Inc for $455 million.
Kraft Foods is a unit of Philip Morris Cos Inc.
The transaction, expected to be completed by year-end, includes Lender's plants in West Haven/New Haven, Conn.; Mattoon, Ill.; and Buffalo, N.Y., the companies said in a joint statement.
Lender's, based in White Plains, N.Y., is a large manufacturer and marketer of frozen, refrigerated, and fresh bagels with annual sales of $275 million.
"Lender's Bagels is a perfect fit for Kellogg Company's fast-growing convenience foods business," said Arnold Langbo, Kellogg chairman and chief executive officer, in a statement.
"Lender's is a strong franchise, but it does not fit with our long-term strategic direction," said Robert Morrison, chairman and chief executive officer of Kraft.
"The sale of Lender's completes our exit from the bakery category and will allow us to concentrate our resources more effectively on our core businesses," Morrison said in the joint statement.
Kraft Foods is the nation's largest packaged food company with revenues of $16 billion.
Kellogg is the world's largest producer of ready-to-eat cereal and a leader in grain-based convenience foods with revenues of $7 billion.
